questions.question: 1. Which of the following best describes a base case in recursion?

explanations.a: Incorrect. That describes recursion, not the base case.
explanations.c: Correct. The base case is where recursion terminates.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Loops are not required for recursion.

questions.question:
2. What is the output of the following recursive function call: factorial(3)?
function factorial(n) { if (n == 0) return 1; else return n * factorial(n-1); }

explanations.b: Incorrect. 1 is the base case result.
explanations.c: Incorrect. 3 is not the result of factorial(3).

questions.question: 3. Which of the following is NOT a property of recursion?

answers.c: Can be used to solve combinatorial problems

explanations.a: Incorrect. Recursion is not always faster than iteration.
explanations.b: Correct. Recursion requires a base case.
explanations.c: Correct. Recursion is used in combinatorial problems.
explanations.d: Correct. Stack overflow is a risk in recursion.

questions.question: 4. In the context of recursion, what is a call stack overflow?

answers.a: When a function returns a value
answers.c: When too many recursive calls exhaust the stack memory
answers.d: When a variable is not initialized

explanations.a: Incorrect. Returning a value does not cause overflow.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Infinite loops are not stack overflows.
explanations.c: Correct. Too many recursive calls can exhaust stack memory.

questions.question: 5. Which of the following problems is best solved using recursion?

answers.c: Finding the maximum in an array

explanations.a: Incorrect. Assignment does not require recursion.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Addition is a simple operation.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Maximum can be found iteratively.
explanations.d: Correct. Tower of Hanoi is a classic recursive problem.

questions.question: 6. What is the main advantage of tail recursion?

answers.b: It can be optimized to use less stack space

explanations.b: Correct. Tail recursion can be optimized by compilers.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Base case is still required.

questions.question: 7. Which of the following recursive algorithms is used to solve the balancing weights problem?

answers.c: Exploring all combinations of placing weights
answers.d: Adding all weights to one side

explanations.b: Incorrect. Ignoring weights does not solve the problem.
explanations.c: Correct. The recursive solution explores all combinations.
explanations.d: Incorrect. All weights on one side is not the only solution.

questions.question: 8. Which of the following is true about the subset sum problem in recursion?

answers.a: It only works for two weights
answers.b: It is not related to recursion
answers.d: It can be solved by considering all combinations recursively

explanations.a: Incorrect. It works for any number of weights.
explanations.b: Incorrect. It is related to recursion.
explanations.c: Incorrect. It can be solved recursively.
explanations.d: Correct. Subset sum is a classic recursive problem.

questions.question: 9. What is the main risk of using recursion without careful design?

explanations.a: Correct. All are risks of poor recursion design.
explanations.b: Correct. Stack overflow is a risk.

questions.question: 10. Which of the following is NOT a typical use case for recursion?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Assignment does not require recursion.
explanations.c: Correct. Combinatorial problems often use recursion.
explanations.d: Correct. Tree traversal is a classic use of recursion.
